message.content:
**Allele frequency of rs7412 (the APOE ε2 variant) in Europeans**

| Source | Population | Allele frequency (C allele) |
|--------|------------|------------------------------|
| 1000 Genomes Project (Phase 3) | EUR (European) | **≈ 0.12** (12 %) |
| gnomAD v2.1.1 | Non‑Finnish European | **≈ 0.11–0.13** (11–13 %) |
| gnomAD v3.1.1 | European (all) | **≈ 0.12** (12 %) |

> **Interpretation**  
> The C allele at rs7412 corresponds to the APOE ε2 allele. In most European sub‑populations (e.g., Northern, Southern, Central Europe) the allele frequency hovers around 10–13 %. Minor deviations exist (e.g., Finnish populations show slightly lower frequencies), but the overall European average remains close to 12 %.

> **Why it matters**  
> APOE ε2 is associated with a reduced risk of late‑onset Alzheimer’s disease and a lower LDL‑cholesterol level compared with the ε3 allele, but it can increase the risk of type III hyperlipoproteinemia. Knowing its frequency helps in population‑based risk assessments and in designing genetic studies.

> **How the data were derived**  
> The figures come from large, publicly available sequencing datasets (1000 Genomes and gnomAD). They represent aggregated allele counts from thousands of unrelated individuals of European ancestry, providing robust estimates of allele frequency.

---

**Quick reference**  
- **rs7412 C allele frequency in Europeans ≈ 12 %**  
- **Corresponds to APOE ε2 allele**  
- **Useful for genetic epidemiology and risk prediction**
